meta.name: heyfinla.com — Current State
meta.description: Design DNA of the live heyfinla.com marketing site (finla-web repo, branch develop), extracted directly from source (tailwind.config.ts, app/globals.css, component usage counts) rather than screenshot color-measurement — the hex values below are literal, not estimated, since we have the source of truth.
source_references: components/*.tsx (grep survey of rounded-/shadow-/text-[ utility usage)

color.palette_type: monochromatic with a single semantic-green accent

primary.role: ink — primary text, primary buttons, focus rings

accent.role: green (bright #22C55E, dark #15803D, soft #E8F7EE) — success states, positive tool-call chips, CTA emphasis inside the chat demo

neutral.usage: paper→surface→line for backgrounds/dividers (light end), faint→muted for secondary/tertiary text, ink for primary text and dark-mode surfaces (line-dark #242424 for dark-section borders)

color.contrast_strategy: high-contrast dark-on-light dominant; one dark (Tech) section inverts to ink background with white/40 muted text for variety

font_families.heading: Inter (var(--font-inter)) — README claims 'Space Grotesk + Inter' but only Inter is wired in code; a stale doc, not an actual second family
font_families.body: Inter, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, SF Pro Display, Segoe UI, system-ui
font_families.mono: none defined — no monospace token exists despite the product being tool-call/code-adjacent

typography.font_style_notes: single-family system: geometric-humanist sans (Inter) doing all the work, from 84px display down to 5px micro-labels inside the ChatDemo phone mockup (an extreme range — 5px to 84px, ~17x) via arbitrary Tailwind bracket values rather than a formal scale. font-feature-settings 'cv11','ss01' enabled (Inter's single-story a / straight-leg alternates) for an SF-Pro-adjacent feel.

spacing.scale: Tailwind default scale, no custom overrides
spacing.content_density: comfortable on marketing sections, extremely compact inside ChatDemo's simulated iPhone UI (5–13px text, tight padding to mimic real app chrome)
spacing.section_rhythm: consistent generous vertical rhythm between major sections (Nav/Hero/Marquee/HowItWorks/Features/Showcase/Tech/Security/Audience/Faq/Footer), wrap max-width 76rem (1216px) with responsive gutters px-5→px-8→px-10

layout.grid_system: single centered column (.wrap) with internal flex/grid per section, no strict multi-column editorial grid
layout.columns: varies by section (2-col bento in Features, 3-col in HowItWorks/Audience)

border_radius.large: rounded-2xl/3xl and arbitrary 2rem–3.2rem — phone mockup frames, hero panels
border_radius.pill: rounded-full — dominant pattern (55 occurrences: nav pills, buttons, avatar/status dots, tags)

shape.border_usage: subtle 1px (border-line #E7E7E4), occasional border-[1.5px] on emphasis; no bold/thick borders
shape.divider_style: hairline border-b/border-t in border-line, border-line/70 for lower-emphasis dividers

elevation.shadow_style: soft diffused, large-blur negative-spread — cinematic depth on hero/phone-mockup elements only; flat elsewhere

levels.high: shadow-[0_60px_120px_-30px_rgba(10,10,10,0.45),0_25px_50px_-20px_rgba(10,10,10,0.3)] — hero phone mockup, stacked dual-shadow for depth

elevation.depth_cues: shadows on 'device' elements (phone mockups) only; flat surfaces for everything else — depth is reserved to sell the 'this is a real app' illusion of ChatDemo/Showcase

iconography.style: not surveyed in detail (no icon library detected in package.json beyond inline SVG) — likely hand-drawn inline SVG for chips/checkmarks/spinners
iconography.stroke_weight: thin-medium, consistent with hairline border language
iconography.size_scale: small (12–20px), matched to compact chat-UI density
iconography.preferred_set: custom inline SVG, no Lucide/Heroicons dependency found

motion.easing: cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) — signature 'ease-out-expo-ish' curve used consistently for rise/pop/reveal
motion.entrance_pattern: fade + translateY(14–26px) on scroll (IntersectionObserver via Reveal.tsx), staggered via --reveal-delay
motion.exit_pattern: none observed — mostly one-directional reveal, no exit choreography
motion.philosophy: minimal functional with one deliberately playful pocket: ChatDemo's typewriter + thinking-dots + tool-call spinner→checkmark sequence, which carries almost all the site's personality

components.button_style: pill (rounded-full), solid ink-on-paper primary / outline-line secondary, no gradient fills
components.input_style: not heavily used (no live form — CTAs link out to a Google Form)
components.card_style: rounded-xl/2xl, surface or white background, hairline border-line, shadow-sm at most
components.navigation_pattern: sticky top nav with hash-anchor links + pill CTA button
components.modal_style: ChatDemo's slide-out side menu is the closest analog — full-height panel, shadow-[8px_0_32px_rgba(0,0,0,0.18)]
components.list_style: simple stacked rows inside phone-mockup UI (inbox/outbox), FAQ as native <details>/<summary>
components.component_notes: ChatDemo.tsx is the load-bearing component: a fully-simulated iPhone frame (bg-ink chrome) containing a scripted, multi-scenario chat with typewriter text, bouncing 'thinking' dots, tool-call chips that animate spinner→checkmark (musteri_bul, vergi_kontrol, fatura_olustur…), and structured reply cards — this is where ~80% of the site's micro-typography (5–13px) and motion budget lives.

aesthetic.visual_metaphor: a real iPhone Messages/Notes app, not a dashboard — the product performs as software you already know how to use
aesthetic.era_influence: post-2020 Apple/SF-Pro flat minimalism (tight tracking, monochrome, pill controls) crossed with early-2020s dev-tool aesthetics (tool-call chips read like an agent trace/terminal log)
aesthetic.genre: indie-confident fintech / dev-tool-adjacent SaaS — closer to Linear/Cursor than to a bank

visual_language.complexity: moderate — simple monochrome shell, but the ChatDemo interior is detail-rich
visual_language.ornamentation: subtle accents only (dotted bg-grid behind hero, hairline dividers, one green accent) — no decorative illustration
visual_language.whitespace_usage: generous between marketing sections, deliberately compact inside the simulated app UI (for realism)
visual_language.visual_weight_distribution: concentrated on the ChatDemo hero device; supporting sections are lighter/flatter by comparison
visual_language.focal_strategy: single hero element (the phone) carries the pitch; everything below reinforces it
visual_language.contrast_level: high (near-black ink on near-white paper), one full-inversion dark section (Tech) for rhythm
visual_language.texture_usage: none beyond the faint radial-dot bg-grid

composition.hierarchy_method: scale contrast (84px→11px range) plus spatial isolation of the hero device
composition.flow_direction: top-to-bottom single narrative, no diagonal or scattered composition
composition.grouping_strategy: section-by-section blocks separated by generous vertical rhythm and occasional hairline dividers
composition.negative_space_role: lets the phone-mockup detail read as premium rather than cluttered

imagery.photo_treatment: none — no lifestyle photography used; product is represented entirely via simulated UI, not photos
imagery.graphic_elements: dotted radial bg-grid, hairline dividers, small inline SVG icons/checkmarks/spinners
imagery.pattern_usage: minimal — grid texture only behind hero
imagery.image_shape: device-framed rectangles (rounded 2rem–3.2rem) for all product visuals

interaction_feel.feedback_style: state-driven micro-feedback (spinner→checkmark on tool calls, bounce dots while 'thinking')
interaction_feel.hover_behavior: not deeply surveyed — standard opacity/scale nudges expected, e.g. menu-nudge keyframe pulses the menu button to invite discovery
interaction_feel.loading_style: narrative loading — 'thinking' dots and tool-call spinners are staged as part of the story, not generic spinners

brand_voice_in_ui.tone: direct, confident, lightly witty, anti-corporate ('Menü yok, yazışalım.', 'Bodrum'da yazıldı. Kahveyle, tek cümleyle.')
brand_voice_in_ui.formality: informal-professional — second person, contractions, no jargon
brand_voice_in_ui.cta_style: direct imperative ('Erken erişime katıl') — currently routes to an external Google Form (early access, no live signup/app-store yet)
brand_voice_in_ui.empty_state_approach: not applicable — no live app states rendered, only simulated ones
brand_voice_in_ui.error_tone: not observed in current site (no live forms beyond external link)

overview.fallback_strategy: reduce to CSS — prefers-reduced-motion is explicitly respected (globals.css collapses all animation-duration to 0.01ms; ChatDemo/menu-nudge define static reduced-motion fallbacks)
overview.primary_technology: CSS animations + IntersectionObserver (Reveal.tsx) + React state-driven timeline (ChatDemo) — no Canvas/WebGL/GSAP/Three.js anywhere in the stack

background_effects.type: none (dotted radial-gradient grid is static, not animated)
background_effects.description: static faint dot grid behind hero only

scroll_triggered_animations.scrub_behavior: none — binary reveal on enter, not scrubbed to scroll position

text_effects.description: ChatDemo's chat bubbles type on character-by-character with a blinking cursor, timed per scripted scenario

image_effects.description: no image galleries/hover-distortion — all visuals are simulated UI, not photography

svg_animations.description: flow-dash keyframe animates strokeDashoffset on an SVG path (likely a connecting-line/flow diagram in Tech section) for a continuous 'data flowing' cue

visual_effects.composite_notes: The site's entire 'visual effects budget' is spent on ChatDemo's simulated-app choreography (typewriter + bounce-dots + spinner-to-checkmark tool chips + slide-out menu) rather than on ambient decoration (no particles, no WebGL, no parallax). This is a meaningful and consistent restraint: the product's realism argument comes from the UI simulation looking exactly like a real messaging app, not from decorative flourish. Any redesign should preserve this restraint — adding heavy WebGL/particle effects would work against the 'this is real software, not a marketing gimmick' credibility the current site is quietly building.
